insider_note: √x sitting inside a trig function, with no matching 1/√x outside to cancel it, always needs the SQUARING substitution x=t² first — only after that does the integral become an ordinary by-parts question.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Substitute x = t² and integrate by parts
lines: Put √x = t ⇒ x = t² ⇒ dx = 2t dt
I = ∫ cost·2t dt = 2∫ t cost dt
steps.why: Setting √x=t (equivalently x=t²) removes the square root from inside the cosine entirely, turning the integral into 2∫t cost dt — a standard by-parts shape in t.
common_mistakes: Trying to integrate cos√x directly with no substitution, which has no elementary antiderivative in x.
Substituting t=x instead of t=√x, which does not remove the square root.
steps.memory_tip: √x alone (no matching 1/√x) inside a function ⇒ always substitute x=t² first to clear the root.

steps.label: Complete the by-parts and back-substitute for the final answer
steps.why: By-parts with u=t, v=cost gives t sint − ∫sint dt = t sint + cost, and substituting t=√x back in returns the final answer to the original variable x.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to substitute √x back in for t in BOTH terms of the final answer.
Losing the outside factor of 2 picked up from dx=2t dt.
steps.memory_tip: The factor of 2 from dx=2t dt multiplies BOTH terms of the by-parts result, not just one.
